profile_notes: Portrait glass — fast short-tele primes and portrait zooms. GATE: max_aperture <= 2.8 (a fast aperture IS the portrait-lens requirement — subject separation and low-light rendering; f/2.8-or-faster is the honest floor) AND focal_length_mm >= 50 (the classic portrait focal range is 50-135mm; the floor keeps out wide/standard fast zooms and wide primes that would otherwise win on bokeh mentions — a validation run without it put a 16-50 zoom at #1). CAVEAT (documented, lenses-for-wildlife): specs.py resolves focal as a first-number, so a wide-to-normal zoom like 24-70 stores 24 and is EXCLUDED (acceptable — 'best portrait lens' intent wants dedicated short-tele glass, not standard zooms; the honest-door still routes an unresolved focal to pending_backfill, not exclusion). The resulting roster is clean short-tele: 50/85/100/135 primes + 70-200-class tele zooms. CRUX at 3: bokeh — background rendering / subject isolation is to a portrait lens what coma is to an astro lens, the defining criterion. SECONDARY at 2: optical_performance (portraits want sharp-where-it-counts, eyes tack-sharp) and color_rendition (skin-tone rendering). SUPPORTING at 1: chromatic_aberration (purple fringing on high-contrast edges like backlit hair is a classic fast-prime failure), af_performance (eye-AF speed on the lens side), handling (weight/balance for sessions). Deliberately UNWEIGHTED: coma, vignetting, distortion, filter_thread, build — real but not portrait differentiators. gear_class excludes novelty only. DISTINCT-FINGERPRINT CHECK: differs from street lenses (optical 3, focal<=50 gate — the OPPOSITE focal band) and astro lenses (coma 3) by leading with bokeh and gating the long/fast end. Ratified by Lee 2026-09-15.
